To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
thyroid hormone (T3) decreases thyroid hormone receptor (TR)/retinoic acid (RAR) heterodimer, but does not affect TR/retinoid x receptor (RXR) heterodimer binding, to DNA.
triiodothy-ronine (T 3) decreased thyroid hormone receptor (TR)/retinoic acid re-ceptor (RAR) heterodimer binding, but not TR/retinoid x receptor (RXR) heterodimer bind- ing, to DNA.
T3 decreased TR homodimers, but increased TR/RXR heteromers bound to DNA, and that TR/RAR heteromers were not affected by T3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of thyroid hormone receptor function by T3.
the regulation of transcriptional activity of thyroid hormone receptor (TR), retinoic acid receptors (RAR), and retinoid X receptors (RXR).
identifying the receptor complex(es) responsible for thyroid hormone action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ligand binding properties of the TR/RXR heterocomplex is different from the TR/RAR heterocomplex, and the ligand binding of the TR/RAR complex differs from the homodimers.
T3 differentially affects TR/RAR and RXR heterodimer binding.
the ligand-dependent modulation of the DNA-binding affinity of the TR/RAR hetero- dimer is not a general phenomenon and is not necessarily a prerequisite for the regulation of transcription.
